subjective.question: Define a set with examples. A set is a collection of well-defined objects. For example, A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} is a set of numbers, and Z = {0, 1, 2, ...} is the set of integers.

Define a fuzzy set and write its different expressions. A fuzzy set consists of two components: a set and a membership function associated with it. It is written as A~ = {(x, mu_A~(x)) : x in U}, where mu_A~(x) in [0, 1] is the membership value of x. For a finite universe it is expressed as A~ = mu_A~(x1)/x1 + mu_A~(x2)/x2 + ... + mu_A~(xn)/xn = sum of mu_A~(x_i)/x_i, and for a continuous universe as A~ = integral of mu_A~(x)/x over X.

Define the support of a fuzzy set with an example. The support of a fuzzy set A~ is the set of all elements whose membership value is greater than zero, i.e. Support(A~) = {x in X : A~(x) > 0}. Example: if X = {x1, x2, x3, x4} and A~ = {(x1, 0), (x2, 0.1), (x3, 0.5), (x4, 1)}, then Support(A~) = {x2, x3, x4}.

Define an empty fuzzy set with an example. A fuzzy set is said to be an empty fuzzy set if every element maps onto zero, i.e. the membership value of all the elements is zero. Example: for X = {y1, y2, y3}, the fuzzy set A~ = {(y1, 0), (y2, 0), (y3, 0)} is an empty fuzzy set.

Define a normal fuzzy set with an example. A fuzzy set is said to be a normal fuzzy set if there exists at least one element whose membership value is one. Example: for X = {x1, x2, x3}, the fuzzy set A~ = {(x1, 0.8), (x2, 0), (x3, 1)} is normal because x3 has membership value 1.

Define the cardinality of a fuzzy set and find the cardinality of A~ = {(x1, 0.9), (x2, 0.3), (x3, 1)}. The cardinality of a fuzzy set is the sum of the membership values of all its elements. Here |A~| = 0.9 + 0.3 + 1 = 2.2.

Define the union of two fuzzy sets. Let F~(X) denote the collection of fuzzy sets on a universe of discourse X, and let A~, B~ belong to F~(X). The union of A~ and B~ is the fuzzy set C~ = A~ union B~ whose membership function is mu_C~(x) = max{mu_A~(x), mu_B~(x)} = mu_A~(x) OR mu_B~(x), for all x in X.

Define the intersection of two fuzzy sets. Let F~(X) denote the collection of fuzzy sets on X, and let A~, B~ belong to F~(X). The intersection of A~ and B~ is the fuzzy set C~ = A~ intersection B~ whose membership function is mu_C~(x) = min{mu_A~(x), mu_B~(x)} = mu_A~(x) AND mu_B~(x), for all x in X.

Prove that (A~ intersection A~')(x) <= 0.5 for every fuzzy set A~. By the definition of complement, A~'(x) = 1 - A~(x), so (A~ intersection A~')(x) = min(A~(x), 1 - A~(x)). Case 1: if A~(x) <= 0.5, then the minimum is A~(x), which is <= 0.5. Case 2: if A~(x) >= 0.5, then 1 - A~(x) <= 0.5, and the minimum is 1 - A~(x), which is <= 0.5. In both cases (A~ intersection A~')(x) <= 0.5. Hence proved.

Define the degree of subsethood of two fuzzy sets. The degree of subsethood of a fuzzy set A~ in a fuzzy set B~ is defined as S(A~, B~) = |A~ intersection B~| / |A~|, where | . | denotes cardinality. It always lies in the interval [0, 1].

Define the intersection of two intervals. Let I1 = [a1, b1] and I2 = [a2, b2] be two intervals. Their intersection is defined as I1 intersection I2 = [max{a1, a2}, min{b1, b2}]. The intersection is empty if and only if a1 > b2 or a2 > b1.

Let A = {10, 15, 20}. Find A^2 and show it graphically. A^2 = A x A = {10, 15, 20} x {10, 15, 20} = {(10, 10), (10, 15), (10, 20), (15, 10), (15, 15), (15, 20), (20, 10), (20, 15), (20, 20)}. Graphically, A^2 is shown as the nine points of a 3 x 3 grid plotted on the plane at the x- and y-coordinates 10, 15 and 20.

Write the relation R for the following table (rows a1, a2, a3, a4; columns x1, x2, x3): a1: 0, 1, 0; a2: 1, 0, 0; a3: 0, 1, 0; a4: 0, 0, 1. Reading the entries equal to 1 from the table, the relation is R = {(a1, x2), (a2, x1), (a3, x2), (a4, x3)}.

Make the membership table for the fuzzy relation R = {((a, c), 0.7), ((b, a), 0.9), ((c, b), 1), ((c, d), 0.2)}. The membership table M_R (rows and columns a, b, c, d) is: row a: 0, 0, 0.7, 0; row b: 0.9, 0, 0, 0; row c: 0, 1, 0, 0.2; row d: 0, 0, 0, 0. All pairs not listed in R have membership value 0.

Find the fuzzy relation R from the membership table M_R (rows 1, 2, 3; columns a, b, c): row 1: 0.1, 1.0, 0.0; row 2: 0.3, 1.0, 1.0; row 3: 0.0, 1.0, 1.0. Reading each entry of the table as the membership value of the corresponding pair, R = {((1, a), 0.1), ((1, b), 1.0), ((1, c), 0.0), ((2, a), 0.3), ((2, b), 1.0), ((2, c), 1.0), ((3, a), 0.0), ((3, b), 1.0), ((3, c), 1.0)}.

Given the relation tables M_R (rows 1, 2, 3; columns a, b, c): row 1: 0.1, 0.7, 0; row 2: 0, 1, 0.9; row 3: 0.5, 0, 0.2; and S_R: row 1: 1, 0.8, 0.1; row 2: 0.3, 0, 0.5; row 3: 0.9, 1, 0. Find M_{R union S}. The union of two fuzzy relations is obtained by taking the element-wise maximum of their tables. Hence M_{R union S} (rows 1, 2, 3; columns a, b, c) is: row 1: 1, 0.8, 0.1; row 2: 0.3, 1, 0.9; row 3: 0.9, 1, 0.2.
Show that x Delta_4 x = x / (2 - x). As we know, x Delta_4 y = xy / (x + y - xy). Putting y = x, x Delta_4 x = x^2 / (x + x - x^2) = x^2 / (2x - x^2) = x^2 / (x(2 - x)) = x / (2 - x). Hence proved.
Find x Delta_1 x. As we know, x Delta_1 y = 0 OR (x + y - 1) = max(0, x + y - 1). Putting y = x, x Delta_1 x = max(0, x + x - 1) = max(0, 2x - 1).

Prove that X + (Y + Z) = (X + Y) + Z for intervals X, Y and Z. X + (Y + Z) = {x + a : x in X, a in (Y + Z)} = {x + (y + z) : x in X, y in Y, z in Z} = {(x + y) + z : x in X, y in Y, z in Z} = {b + z : b in (X + Y), z in Z} = (X + Y) + Z. Hence proved.

The membership function of a triangular fuzzy number A~ is mu_A~(x) = (x - a)/(b - a) for a <= x <= b, (c - x)/(c - b) for b <= x <= c, and 0 otherwise. The alpha-cut is written as A_alpha = [alpha_1, alpha_2]. Find alpha_1 and alpha_2. On the left side, setting (x - a)/(b - a) = alpha gives alpha(b - a) = x - a, so alpha_1 = x = a + alpha(b - a). On the right side, setting (c - x)/(c - b) = alpha gives c - x = alpha(c - b), so alpha_2 = x = c - alpha(c - b). Hence A_alpha = [a + alpha(b - a), c - alpha(c - b)].

Draw the graph of the triangular fuzzy number whose membership function is mu_A(x) = (x - 3)/(5 - 3) for 3 <= x <= 5, (6 - x)/(6 - 5) for 5 <= x <= 6, and 0 otherwise. The graph is a triangle with vertices at (3, 0), (5, 1) and (6, 0). Starting from 0 at x = 3, the membership value rises linearly along the line (x - 3)/2 until it reaches the peak value 1 at x = 5; it then falls linearly along the line (6 - x)/1 until it reaches 0 at x = 6. The membership value is 0 for all x outside the interval [3, 6].
